{{nihongo|'''Sakamoto Shrine Suwa Shrine'''|諏訪神社 (中津川市茄子川)}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Mino Province]].

'''Suwa Shrine''' (すわじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} enshrined in {{ill|Nasubigawa|ja|茄子川村|qid=Q22126369|lt=Nasubigawa}}, {{ill|Nakatsugawa|Q844052|qid=Q844052}}, {{ill|Gifu Prefecture|ace|Prefektur Gifu|af|Gifu-prefektuur|an|Prefectura de Gifu|ar|غيفو (محافظة)|arz|جيفو (محافظه)|az|Gifu prefekturası|azb|قیفو اوستانی|ban|Préféktur Gifu|be|Гіфу (прэфектура)|bg|Гифу|bn|গিফু প্রশাসনিক অঞ্চল|ca|Prefectura de Gifu|cdo|Gifu-gâing|ce|Гифу (префектура)|ceb|Gifu-ken|ckb|پارێزگای گیفو|cs|Prefektura Gifu|cy|Gifu (talaith)|da|Gifu-præfekturet|de|Präfektur Gifu|eo|Gubernio Gifu|es|Prefectura de Gifu|et|Gifu prefektuur|eu|Gifu (prefektura)|fa|استان گیفو|fi|Gifun prefektuuri|fr|Préfecture de Gifu|frr|Gifu (Prefektüür)|ga|Maoracht Gifu|gl|Prefectura de Gifu|hak|Gifu-yen|he|גיפו (מחוז)|hr|Gifu (prefektura)|hu|Gifu prefektúra|hy|Գիֆու (պրեֆեկտուրա)|id|Prefektur Gifu|ilo|Prepektura ti Gifu|it|Prefettura di Gifu|ja|岐阜県|jv|Préfèktur Gifu|ka|გიფუს პრეფექტურა|kn|ಗಿಫು (ಪ್ರಾಂತ್ಯ)|ko|기후현|lt|Gifu prefektūra|lv|Gifu prefektūra|mk|Гифу (префектура)|mni|ꯒꯤꯐꯨ ꯂꯝꯈꯥꯢ|mr|गिफू प्रांत|ms|Wilayah Gifu|ne|गिफु|nl|Gifu (prefectuur)|no|Gifu (prefektur)|nov|Gifu Prefekture|os|Гифу (префектурæ)|pam|Prepektura ning Gifu|pl|Prefektura Gifu|pnb|ضلع گیفو|pt|Gifu|ro|Prefectura Gifu|ru|Гифу (префектура)|se|Gifu prefektuvra|sh|Prefektura Gifu|simple|Gifu Prefecture|sk|Gifu (prefektúra)|sr|Префектура Гифу|su|Préféktur Gifu|sv|Gifu prefektur|sw|Mkoa wa Gifu|tg|Префектураи Гифу|th|จังหวัดกิฟุ|tl|Prepektura ng Gifu|tr|Gifu (prefektörlük)|tt|Гифу (префектура)|uk|Префектура Ґіфу|ur|گیفو پریفیکچر|vi|Gifu|war|Gifu (prefektura)|wuu|岐阜县|zh|岐阜县|zh_classical|岐阜縣|zh_min_nan|Gihu-koān|zh_yue|岐阜縣|qid=Q131277}}.

It is regarded as Sakamoto Shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shikinaisha entries}} of the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Engishiki Jinmyōchō}}.

=== History ===
This shrine was founded by soliciting from {{ill|Suwa-taisha|abstract|Q218813|de|Suwa-Taisha|es|Suwa taisha|eu|Suwa taisha|fa|زیارتگاه بزرگ سووا|fr|Suwa-taisha|hu|Szuva templom|id|Kuil Suwa|it|Santuario di Suwa (Sohonsha)|ja|諏訪大社|ko|스와 대사|lt|Suvos maldykla|pl|Suwa Taisha|ru|Сува-тайся|simple|Suwa-taisha|tr|Suwa-taisha|zh|諏訪大社|qid=Q218813}} in {{ill|Shinano Province|Q289250|qid=Q289250}}.

Besides this "Sakamoto Shrine Suwa-sha," {{ill|Sakamoto Shrine & Hachimangu|ja|八幡神社 (中津川市千旦林)|qid=Q11391067|lt=Sakamoto Shrine Hachiman-gū}} is also considered for Sakamoto Shrine of {{ill|Mino Province|Q864156|qid=Q864156}} {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}.

According to the history of Sakamoto Shrine Hachiman-gū, Sakamoto Shrine was founded in {{ill|Taihō (era)|Q1346269|qid=Q1346269|lt=Taihō}} 2 ({{ill|702|Q23497|qid=Q23497}}).

In {{ill|Enbun|Q1145071|qid=Q1145071}} 2 ({{ill|1357|Q6135|qid=Q6135}}) of the {{ill|Nanboku-chō period|ar|فترة نانبوكو تشو|bg|Нанбоку-чо|bn|নান্‌বোকু-চোও যুগ|ca|Període Nanboku-chō|cs|Období Nanbokučó|de|Namboku-chō|es|Período Nanbokuchō|eu|Nanboku-chō Aroa|fa|دوره نانبوکوچو|fi|Nanboku-chō-kausi|fr|Époque Nanboku-chō|he|תקופת שתי החצרות הקיסריות|hu|A japán császári udvar különválása|id|Zaman Nanboku-chō|it|Periodo Nanboku-chō|ja|南北朝時代 (日本)|ko|남북조 시대 (일본)|ms|Tempoh Nanboku-chō|nl|Nanboku-cho-periode|pt|Período Nanboku-chō|ru|Период Намбокутё|simple|Nanboku-chō period|sr|Нанбокућо период|sv|Nanboku-chō|th|ยุคราชสำนักเหนือ-ใต้|tr|Nanboku-chō Dönemi|uk|Період Намбокутьо|vi|Nam–Bắc triều (Nhật Bản)|zh|南北朝时代 (日本)|zh_min_nan|Nanboku-tyô sî-tāi|zh_yue|南北朝 (日本)|qid=Q264012|lt=Nanboku-chō period}}, shrine buildings of Sakamoto Shrine burned in a field fire,

and "Sakamoto Shrine Suwa-sha" is said to have relocated and enshrined at the current site.

There is also a theory that Sakamoto Shrine originally stood at the site of "Sakamoto Shrine Hachiman-gū," was destroyed by fire, then moved as "Sakamoto Shrine Suwa-sha," while the rebuilt shrine at the original site became "Sakamoto Shrine Hachiman-gū."

When forces led by {{ill|Takeda Katsuyori|Q662482|qid=Q662482}} invaded {{ill|Tōnō|Q7862707|qid=Q7862707}} in {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} 2 ({{ill|1574|Q6680|qid=Q6680}}), they burned and destroyed temples and shrines in Ena District including Sakamoto Shrine Hachiman-gū, but there are no records or traditions that Sakamoto Shrine Suwa-sha was burned.

One reason is thought to be that the war deity of the {{ill|Takeda clan|Q1210114|qid=Q1210114}} was Suwa Daimyōjin, and Katsuyori's maternal line was the {{ill|Suwa clan|Q2975376|qid=Q2975376}}, hereditary Ōhōri of {{ill|Suwa-taisha|abstract|Q218813|de|Suwa-Taisha|es|Suwa taisha|eu|Suwa taisha|fa|زیارتگاه بزرگ سووا|fr|Suwa-taisha|hu|Szuva templom|id|Kuil Suwa|it|Santuario di Suwa (Sohonsha)|ja|諏訪大社|ko|스와 대사|lt|Suvos maldykla|pl|Suwa Taisha|ru|Сува-тайся|simple|Suwa-taisha|tr|Suwa-taisha|zh|諏訪大社|qid=Q218813}}. Until inheriting the Takeda clan, Katsuyori himself was called Suwa Katsuyori.

In the early {{ill|Meiji era|lt=Meiji period|qid=Q3125096}}, there was debate whether Sakamoto Shrine was Suwa Shrine or Hachiman Shrine, but no conclusion was reached, so both shrines stopped using the name Sakamoto Shrine and adopted "Suwa Shrine" and "Hachiman Shrine" as official names.

Today, as common names, Suwa Shrine is called "Sakamoto Shrine Suwa-sha" and Hachiman Shrine is called "Sakamoto Shrine Hachiman-gū."

=== Transportation ===
* About 5 km from {{ill|Mino-Sakamoto Station|Q5359412|qid=Q5359412}} on the {{ill|Chūō Main Line|Q1078110|qid=Q1078110}}
* {{ill|Kitaena Kotsu|Q11401729|qid=Q11401729}} Nakatsugawa Park Line, get off at "Higashi-Mino Fureai Center-mae" bus stop, then 20 minutes on foot
